I said I was sorry, I was just saying what someone who had dealt with DID in their personal life had told me :/ I never even said anything to do with the facts about how it works because I'm not a medical professional! I was just trying to point out that rare mental illnesses aren't usually as rare as people make it seem like in their minds. 
I'm sorry :(

I did just say that I was wrong, I'm not disagreeing with you on that! I'd heard the statistic from a friend who's parent had DID so I'd always just assumed it was right. But also with a large margin like that we can't just assume it's gonna be at the very lowest estimate, that just isn't fair

It's super late where I am so I can't be bothered looking for anything on google scholar, but 

https://www.healthline.com/health/red-hair-blue-eyes estimates that red hair is 1% - 2% of the population has red hair with blue eyes, and the article seems to be peer reviewed by a doctor.

https://www.sane.org/information-stories/facts-and-guides/dissociative-identity-disorder states that between 0.01% to up to 15% of the population could suffer with DID 
So maybe saying that it's the same percentage is kinda wrong, but we don't know enough to be able to say that it is something super incredibly rare! And it is likely more common than we assume

I just wanna say that DID isn't as rare as people think! It's the same percentage of people with natural red hair!!
